title: Published Interface Delegation Chain (API Freeze)
pattern: A public function marked `#[deprecated]` (or language equivalent) that performs no business logic of its own, but merely delegates arguments directly to a newer function.
why_bad: Indirection bloat. It keeps outdated naming structures alive in public APIs, increasing the cognitive load of the library surface area. It causes "alert fatigue" when compilers warn about usages that the library author could easily have resolved internally with automated tooling.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. A public function with a deprecation attribute (`#[deprecated]`).
2. The function body consists entirely of a direct forwarding call (optionally mapping parameter structures) to another public/private function.
source:
- Martin Fowler, *Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code* (1999) [171, 736]
- Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020) [Chapter 15, Deprecation]
